---
title: "Releasing"
subtitle: "From a commit on main to zips users can download"
---

A release is a **version tag**. Pushing a tag that starts with `v` builds the
application for every platform and publishes a GitHub Release with one zip per
platform. Ordinary pushes to `main` build nothing.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
`modboard.spec` is the PyInstaller recipe and
`.github/workflows/release.yml` the workflow. Nothing on GitHub needs setting
up: the workflow asks for the write permission it needs itself.
:::

## Release a new version

1. Make sure `main` is pushed and works from source: `uv run python app.py`.
2. Bump `version` in `pyproject.toml`, for example `0.1.0` → `0.2.0`, then commit
   and push.
3. Optional: build without releasing. **Actions → Release → Run workflow**
   builds the three zips and attaches them to the run under **Artifacts**. No
   release is created.
4. Tag the same version and push the tag:

   ```bash
   git tag v0.2.0
   git push origin v0.2.0
   ```

5. Wait for the run under **Actions** (about 5 minutes). The Release appears
   under **Releases** with generated notes and these files:

   | File | For |
   |---|---|
   | `modboard-windows-x64.zip` | Windows |
   | `modboard-macos-arm64.zip` | Macs with Apple Silicon (M1 and later) |
   | `modboard-macos-x64.zip` | Macs with Intel |

The README links to `releases/latest`, so it points at the new version without
an edit.

## What the workflow does

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  T["push tag v*"] --> W["build on windows-latest"]
  T --> A["build on macos-latest (arm64)"]
  T --> I["build on macos-15-intel (x64)"]
  W --> R["release: publish the zips"]
  A --> R
  I --> R
```

PyInstaller does not cross-compile, so each platform builds on its own runner:
`uv sync --locked`, then `pyinstaller modboard.spec`, then a zip. The
**release** job only runs for a tag; a manual run stops after the builds.

## Building locally

```bash
uv run pyinstaller modboard.spec --noconfirm   # -> dist/modboard
```

The result is one executable for the machine it was built on. It does not
pick up later source edits: rebuild after every change. It keeps its data in
`~/Library/Application Support/Modboard` (macOS) or `%APPDATA%\Modboard`
(Windows), not in the repository; see `DATA_DIR` in `src/config.py`.

Two macOS details while testing a local build:

- **Keychain prompts.** Secrets saved while running from source belong to
  Python, so the build asks before reading them. Each rebuild is a new,
  ad-hoc-signed program, and "Always Allow" does not carry over. Run from
  source while developing.
- **No Gatekeeper warning.** A local build is not marked as downloaded. To see
  what users see, download the zip from a workflow run.

## If something goes wrong

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| A tag was pushed for the wrong commit | Delete the Release on GitHub, then `git push --delete origin v0.2.0` and `git tag -d v0.2.0`, and tag again |
| `uv sync --locked` fails | `uv.lock` is out of date: run `uv lock`, commit, push, tag again |
| The **release** job fails with `403` | **Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → Read and write** |
| The build succeeds but the app cannot find a template or file | It is missing from `datas` in `modboard.spec` |
